title: Multi-Ion Plasma FIB for Advanced TEM Lamella Preparation: A Comparative Study Toward (SE)EBIC-Enabled Analysis
content: Ga-based Focused Ion Beam (FIB) systems are widely used for TEM lamella preparation, but undesired Ga incorporation can modify critical properties of the specimen (e.g., electrical behavior) [1]. Consequently, alternative plasma-FIB (PFIB) sources, such as Xe+ or Ar+, have become attractive for producing high-quality, electron-transparent lamellae [2]. A critical yet sometimes overlooked step in the in situ lift-out process is the protective-layer deposition. Here the thickness, uniformity, and composition can affect the subsequent FIB processing steps, including curtaining and beam-induced damage [3]. Furthermore, emerging Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (STEM) techniques such as (Secondary Electron) Electron Beam-Induced Current ((SE)EBIC) [4–6] demand carefully optimized lamella preparation to minimize artifacts and accurately probe conduction pathways at high spatial resolution.
